n1: The node’s binding is ambiguous and appears to select the wrong object: the source image shows a small square DVD case near the center and a separate black object to its right, while the edited image shows two white discs. The traces repeatedly call the right-hand disc the DVD and report it white, but do not establish that it is the DVD referenced by the instruction; the central case/disc may instead be the target, and the edit may have introduced or transformed objects. Refine the binding to identify the DVD using its source-image location and appearance, then compare that same object across source and edited images. The criterion should distinguish complete whitening from partial color change and no progress, while allowing unknown if identity or visual evidence is insufficient. Do not treat repeated high-confidence traces as independent confirmation: they share the same apparent target-selection error. This is a semantic grounding issue, not a transport or dependency failure.

The binding is truncated/ambiguous (“near (...) case near the center”) and should identify the source target precisely, then require tracking that same object into the edited image—not treating a nearby white object as evidence. The images show the small square case near the center in the source is absent in the edit; a white circular disc appears nearby, but its proximity does not establish identity or a color change. Keep the criterion’s distinction between absent progress and partial progress: partial requires visual evidence that the same target changed toward white, not merely that it disappeared while a white disc appeared. The repeated traces are valid, queried, high-confidence, and dependency-free, so this is not a transport/schema failure; their partial/no split indicates criterion application ambiguity. Clarify that disappearance or replacement without evidence of continuity is not progress, while preserving an unresolved outcome if identity/change genuinely cannot be determined. Do not infer fulfillment from the reference label alone.

Thus disappearance alone is not progress, and the repeated traces’ “partial” labels conflict with their own evidence and the rubric; reserve partial for an evidenced change to the same DVD toward white, and use unknown if identity/change cannot be established.
